_comment: Per-scene object list for the clear-the-table task. Keyed by --scene. Each entry names a YCB object (built into assets/ycb_mjcf/ by scripts/build_ycb.py) and its table-top XY. z is auto-derived from the object's rest height + the scene's table-top (TABLE_TOP_Z). Optional per-entry: quat (4), mass (kg), friction (3), solref (2). ~5 objects per scene is typical. The CLI --objects flag OVERRIDES this list; if this file (or a scene's entry) is missing, the loader falls back to the primitive obj_* bodies authored in the scene XML.
_comment_solref: Per-object contact COMPLIANCE = solref [time_constant, damping_ratio], set from the object's REAL material. Default (omitted) = [0.004, 1] = rigid (0.004s is the stability floor at dt=2ms; can't go stiffer, rests flush on the table). Larger time-constant = softer/more give (always stable, it's above the floor). Assignments here: RIGID (0.004, omitted) = 036_wood_block (solid wood), 058_golf_ball (hard resin), 025_mug (ceramic). DEFORMABLE: 009_gelatin_box is a thin CARDBOARD Jell-O carton (soft, ~0.012), 056_tennis_ball rubber+felt (springy, ~0.013), 017_orange soft fruit (~0.010), 014_lemon firm fruit (~0.007).
_comment_scope: Mesh objects are for the plain-teleop dexpilot / anyteleop modes (grasp by hand physics, no recommender). Contact-aware modes need per-object grasp-contact handling for meshes (in progress) and stay on the primitive stand-ins.
_comment_layout: Base yawed +90 deg, arm reaching +y (across the table WIDTH). Objects are spread along the table LENGTH (world x, from -0.30 to +0.30) in FRONT of the arm (+y ~0.30-0.34), so the operator picks them left-to-right along the length. All 0.30-0.42 m from the base (reachable, none under the robot) and >=0.05 m inside the table edges (x in [-0.55,0.55], y in [-0.075,0.575]).
_comment_wood_block: 036_wood_block is laid HORIZONTAL (long axis along the table length, x) via quat [0.7071,0,-0.7071,0] = -90deg about world y, which maps its local long (z) axis to +x. Laid flat it spans ~21cm(x) x 14cm(y); placed in its own clear lane so it doesn't collide with the other objects.
